precepts.text: Build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them; that is the wealth the Most High teaches.
precepts.point: We have to be retaught what wealth is: build houses, dwell in them, plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them, and learn to provide for ourselves.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.” When the scriptures speak of our forefathers being rich, it is not carnal wealth. Abram was rich in livestock, land, and the things that take care of a family; that is true wealth.

We have to be retaught what wealth is: “Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.” Build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them, and learn to provide for ourselves. That is the wealth the Most High teaches.

precepts.text: Haran begat Lot; Lot was Abram's nephew.
precepts.point: Their substance was so great they could not dwell together. That substance came from Egypt, where Pharaoh entreated Abram well for Sarai's sake and gave him sheep, oxen, servants, and camels; the maidservants from Egypt are where Hagar comes from.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
Lot was Abram’s nephew. “Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran begat Lot.” Haran was Abram’s brother, so Lot, the son of Haran, is the brother’s son who went with Abram.

That is who is in the strife of Genesis 13. Lot “also, which went with Abram, had flocks, and herds, and tents”, and the two households, uncle and nephew, had grown so great that “the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together.”

precepts.text: Pharaoh gave Abram livestock and menservants and maidservants; this is where the household's wealth and Hagar came from.
precepts.point: Their substance was so great they could not dwell together. That substance came from Egypt, where Pharaoh entreated Abram well for Sarai's sake and gave him sheep, oxen, servants, and camels; the maidservants from Egypt are where Hagar comes from.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
Where did all that substance come from? Egypt. When Sarai was taken into Pharaoh’s house, Pharaoh “entreated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he asses, and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.”

That is the wealth of the household in Genesis 13: “their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.” The flocks and herds that the herdmen of Abram and the herdmen of Lot strove over were the livestock Pharaoh gave for Sarai’s sake.

The maidservants from Egypt matter too. That is where Hagar comes from: an Egyptian maidservant brought into the household when Pharaoh gave Abram menservants and maidservants.

precepts.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God; Abram was a peacemaker.
precepts.point: Be solution minded and fix problems using the scriptures; blessed are the peacemakers.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” Abram was a peacemaker. When the herdmen strove, he said, “Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.”

That was the spirit of Abram: he would de-escalate and look for solutions. “Is not the whole land before thee?” If you go left I go right; if you go right I go left. You cannot argue with that.

Be solution minded and fix problems using the scriptures. The peacemaker is called a child of God, and Abram showed how it is done: not by winning the argument, but by ending the strife between brethren.

precepts.text: Lot dwelt in Sodom; pitching toward Sodom ended with dwelling in it.
precepts.point: The men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly: they were lawless, without principles, and given to sexual freedom. That is why the city was overthrown.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
Lot “pitched his tent toward Sodom.” One chapter later, when the kings came against the cities of the plain, “they took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.” Toward Sodom became in Sodom.

Lot lifted up his eyes and chose the plain of Jordan because it was well watered every where, fertile “as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt.” But “the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly”: lawless, without principles, and given to sexual freedom. That is why the city was overthrown.

He pitched toward that city, and he ended up dwelling in it, and he was carried away captive with it. That is where pitching toward Sodom leads.

precepts.text: Unto thy seed will I give this land; the promise was made at Abram's first altar.
precepts.point: This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
This is the Most High reiterating the promise He made when Abram first entered the land. Back then “the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land”, and Abram built his first altar there to the Lord who appeared to him.

Now, after Lot was separated from him, the Lord tells him to look northward, southward, eastward and westward: “all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.” Same promise, same land, spoken again with the whole length and breadth of it laid out before him.

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; they shall be called the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered.” That is covenant language, and it is the same language spoken over the children of Israel: “the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

The seed of Abram that cannot be numbered is the children of Israel. And Hosea says where that seed ends up: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The promise to Abram’s seed as the dust of the earth is the promise to Israel, the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain and pitched toward Sodom; his dwelling there is why Abraham interceded.
precepts.point: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
Why did Abraham draw near and negotiate with the Most High over Sodom? Because his nephew was there. “Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelled in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom.”

Lot’s dwelling there is why Abraham pleaded for the city. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” He reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty and ten, and the Lord said, “I will not destroy it for ten’s sake.” Below ten there was no more negotiating; the Lord went His way, and Abraham returned unto his place.

points: Abram was very rich in cattle, silver and gold; rich in the Bible with those things means wealthy.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: The Most High is promising Abraham this land, but there were already people in the land: the Canaanites, the descendants of Canaan. So were Abraham and the Israelites just going to take a land that belonged to another people? No.

Abraham is now dwelling in the land of Canaan, the land the Lord promised to give unto him and his seed. Lift up now thine eyes northward, southward, eastward, and westward: all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.

Before the flood, the sons of God were living in that land; that is the land Adam and his sons were given. When God flooded the earth, Canaan went back and settled that land; Shem did not. Shem stayed over in the Chaldees, and Shem is the chosen lineage the sons of God came back through. So when the sons of God came back, the Lord was giving them back the land they dwelt in before the flood.

When the scriptures speak of our forefathers being rich, it is not carnal wealth. Abram was rich in cattle, silver, and gold: livestock, land, and the things that take care of a family. That is true wealth.
